quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean as the operator leans. They should sit as close to the front as possible without getting in the operator's way. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle sits lower with a passenger's extra weight. Ride a bit more slowly than usual, especially through curves, corners, and over bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, or stop. Keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From a library book about motorcycles.

questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source of information about your specific motorcycle. Read the manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down where other drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or when approaching an alley.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep your motorcycle straight. Gradually apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: If you lock your rear wheel while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How should you brake if you are in a curve?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning than when it is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: By changing power suddenly in a turn.
While riding the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride closely to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on to improve visibility. Choose a lane position that gives oncoming traffic a good view of your motorcycle. Keep enough space to react if something goes wrong. Do not assume eye contact with a driver means they see you.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly on wet pavement?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on slippery pavement. You can use the front brake on slippery surfaces if you apply it gradually to avoid locking it.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield cannot replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: You should inspect your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
Using both the front and rear brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: To stop in the shortest distance on a straight road, use both brakes. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will properly yield to you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not guarantee the other driver will properly yield to you.
Means that the other driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the other driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will properly yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good way for a rider to increase their visibility?

options.text: Using their headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible to other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance at night.
You should always maintain the same following distance regardless of the time of day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you lose visual cues like shadows and light contrasts. Allow a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: When traveling on a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: Your passenger should ride in the sidecar. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: To safely ride on a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to brake.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol while taking them.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your ability to ride safely. This includes over-the-counter medications, prescription medications, and illegal drugs. They work like alcohol.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Practice on a quiet road first. Your motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. You need to get used to the extra weight before riding in traffic.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, it is best to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles and at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
